title: Pressure? Dimensional Formula Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A doctor reads blood pressure, a tyre shop checks air pressure, a diver feels water pressure. Diya's pressure cooker whistles when the steam pushes hard enough. But what is pressure made of, in mass, length and time? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement, section 1.5) we learn dimensional formulae and dimensional equations.

Watch the cooker lid on a live motion notebook: the force on the vent grows, the weight lifts in a slow-mo replay, and the pressure graph climbs and drops with every whistle. Then we build pressure block by block: velocity [LT⁻¹], acceleration [LT⁻²], force [MLT⁻²], area [L²], pressure [ML⁻¹T⁻²], and check each power link by link. Force vs pressure side by side, work and kinetic energy [ML²T⁻²], a worked example for power [ML²T⁻³], the missing-minus exam trap, an original NEET pattern question on surface tension, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Three pressures, one question
0:26 What a dimensional formula and a dimensional equation are
0:53 The cooker lid: force, area and pressure, live
1:28 Pressure, block by block: v, a, F, A, P
2:04 Each power, link by link
2:35 Force vs pressure + pause and think
3:08 Work and kinetic energy: [ML²T⁻²]
3:44 Worked example: power [ML²T⁻³]
4:13 Exam trap: the missing minus sign
4:36 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:06 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Principle of Dimensional Homogeneity. Can dimensions prove a formula wrong in one line?
